messages:
Support: FYI we have an escalation from AcmeCorp — intermittent 401s on signed API requests during a key rotation window. They see bursts of failed signature verification for ~30s after we rotate keys.

Sam: can you paste an example request/response? are they using our hosted JWKS (/.well-known/jwks.json) or a custom idp?

Support: hosted JWKS. Here is the log from our edge (redacted):
```
[2026-03-12T15:02:41Z] verify_signature: kid=K1234 failed -> signature mismatch
[2026-03-12T15:02:42Z] jwks_cache: last_refresh=2026-03-12T14:59:58Z ttl=120s -> serving cached keys
[2026-03-12T15:03:10Z] verify_signature: kid=K5678 ok
```
And a sample failing curl:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_signature","detail":"kid K1234 not valid"}
```

Maria: this looks like a classic rotation vs cache TTL race. Do we push new keyset with updated kid K5678, but some edge nodes still have cached jwks.json with K1234 only? Any CDN cache-control on jwks.json?

Support: checking headers from the edge: `curl -I https://auth.redwood.ai/.well-known/jwks.json` returns: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: max-age=120
Age: 58
```
So some nodes are returning the older payload while rotation is in flight.

Sam: yep. Our jwks cache code polls every TTL (120s) and updates atomically. If rotation happens just after a poll, nodes will serve stale keys until next refresh. For signing we rotate active kid immediately; verifying nodes rely on cached jwks. That creates a 0–TTL window where tokens signed with new kid fail.

Jia: two quick mitigations: (1) when we rotate, publish the new jwks.json with both old and new keys for a short overlap window; (2) add short leeway in verifier to fallback to a background fetch if kid not found. Which is easier short-term?

Sam: easiest short-term is fallback fetch: when verify sees an unknown kid, trigger async fetch+verify retry (but sync-blocking fallback for one retry would reduce the 401s). Longer-term we should ensure rotation writes include both keys for at least 60s and set Cache-Control appropriately.

Support: can we reproduce reliably? Here's a minimal repro I used against staging:
1) rotate signing key (staging) -> new kid K8901 active
2) immediately send a signed request using K8901 from test client
3) edge responds 401 for ~20–45s, then succeeds.

Repro curl (staging):
```
# after rotation trigger
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-signed-with-K8901>" https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
Edge log: `jwks_cache: ttl_remaining=3s; verify: kid not found; triggered refresh; retry ok`

Maria: also check CDN and intermediate caching. If CloudFront or a CDN caches jwks.json, the Age header and max-age matter. We should set `Cache-Control: max-age=5, stale-while-revalidate=60` maybe, and publish overlapping keys on rotation. That lets nodes serve old+new keys quickly.

Sam: agree. Implementation plan:
- short term: implement verify fallback -> if kid missing, do a blocking refresh + single retry (safe, low QPS) (owner: Sam)
- short term: update rotation process to publish jwks with both old & new keys for 60s (owner: Maria)
- medium term: adjust CDN cache policy to low max-age + stale-while-revalidate (owner: infra)

Jia: add tests to exercise race windows in unit/integration: simulate TTL boundary, simulate Age>TTL on header, ensure verifier triggers refresh. I'll add a test harness.

Support: opened ticket INC-4421 and notified AcmeCorp support contact. cc @Sam @Maria. Customer impact: intermittent 401s during rotation only; no leaked keys.

ops-bot: created internal issue #SEC-2026 and scheduled a postmortem doc stub.

deploy-bot: deploying jwks fetch-fallback patch to staging now (build 5482). Rolling to canary.

Sam: patch is live on staging canary — pls validate by running repro.

Support: ran the repro 5x in a row — all succeeded (no 401s). Collecting logs to send to customer.

Maria: I'll coordinate to change rotation flow to include overlapping keys and update the rotation playbook. Also adding a note in runbook about verifying Cache-Control on jwks endpoints.

Jia: I'll commit tests and a small harness for future regressions.

Support: thanks team — will keep customer updated and close INC-4421 after prod deploy and one business day of stability. :thumbsup:
